\subsection{The limit tracks repetition, not length}

Figure~\ref{fig:main}(a) is the paper's sharpest test. Each control carries its
twin's carrier and word count, the $k$ copies of one word becoming non-adjacent
distinct ones; were the failure about length, attention span, exposure bias or a
duration budget the two curves would coincide. They do not. Below $k\!=\!6$ every model is
essentially exact; above it, repeated items are rendered with a median count
error of \ErrRepCk{}\% per checkpoint against \ErrCtl{}\%
$[\ErrCtlLo{},\ErrCtlHi{}]$ for controls ($n=\ErrCtlN{}$), at every $k$ to $32$
and for every model. The contrast is sharpest in exactly-correct renderings:
\ExactRep{}\% for repeated items against \ExactCtl{}\% for their controls.

\emph{Our \NModels{} checkpoints are only \NFamilies{} architecture families},
so we model the clustering rather than count checkpoints. By family the gap is
\FamExact{} $[\FamExactLo{},\FamExactHi{}]$ points, all three positive; by
checkpoint \CkExact{} $[\CkExactLo{},\CkExactHi{}]$, positive in all
\CkExactNPos{} --- including the one whose median-error gap is zero, which still
renders repeated items exactly \CkRevExact{} points less often than its controls
(Table~\ref{tab:models}). A mixed-effects linear probability model with
architecture as a random effect and checkpoint nested inside it puts the gap at
\MixArm{} points, and \MixAllClear{} six interval constructions exclude zero,
the widest being $[\MixLo{},\MixHi{}]$. Partial pooling puts the posterior
predictive gap for an architecture \emph{outside} the panel at \BayesNewFam{}
$[\BayesNewFamLo{},\BayesNewFamHi{}]$, but three groups barely identify a
group-level scale and under the widest prior on it that gap touches zero
($\BayesWidePriorLo{}$), so we did not rest on the extrapolation: we tested it.
CosyVoice~2, whose alignment supervision makes it the design most likely to be
immune, renders repeated text exactly \CosyRep{}\% against \CosyCtl{}\% for its
controls ($n=\CosyN{}$): a gap of \CosyGap{} points, inside the predicted
interval and nearer its \BayesNewFam{} mean than an interval that wide entitles
us to expect, from a fit committed before that checkpoint existed (S16). Across \SpecN{} specifications
over six analysis axes --- exclusions, $k$ threshold, cycled against
never-cycled controls, seed subset, aggregation and outcome definition --- the
gap runs \SpecLo{}--\SpecHi{} points, median \SpecMed{}, and none reverses its
sign. The judge and the counting rule are varied in S14 and S28, not here. These are not independent tests and we correct across none: the curve is a
robustness envelope over one comparison, not a family of hypotheses, and our
claims rest on effect sizes (S11).

\emph{Periodicity, or verbatim identity?} The two vary together above, so we ran
a ladder holding carrier, word count and requested count fixed and varying only
the period $p$. The deficit is \emph{graded}: exact rates rise \PerPOne{},
\PerPTwo{}, \PerPFour{}, \PerPEight{}\% at $p=1,2,4,8$, monotone in all
\PerNCk{} checkpoints ($n=\PerNKept{}$). The decisive cell is $p\!=\!2$, where no token
is ever adjacent to itself and half the deficit remains: \PerDTwo{} against
\PerDOne{} points, a surviving fraction of \PerRatioScan{} on the
strictest of \PerNRules{} rules and \PerRatioRecLo{}--\PerRatioRecHi{} on the
others (S28). Nor a power-of-two artifact: re-measured at $k{=}\OddK{}$,
the \emph{odd} rung (\OddPThree{}\%) and the non-power-of-two $p{=}6$
(\OddPSix{}\%) both land between their neighbours \emph{on that ladder}, both
pre-committed tests passing in all \OddLooPass{} leave-one-out fits, only the
saturated top rung not clearing zero (S28). Nor a failure to tell neighbours
apart: a comma, full stop or ``and'' between repetitions recovers none of it
($n{=}\DisN{}$).

\emph{Does the \textbf{ordering} carry it?} Only $p\!=\!4$ can ask: at $p\!=\!2$
the unique zero-adjacency arrangement \emph{is} the alternation, so any shuffle
reintroduces adjacent repeats (rate \ShufAdjRate{}), and $p\!=\!8$ has no deficit
left. Shuffling each item's own multiset recovers \ShufRPct{}\% of a
\ShufDeficit{}-point deficit, missing the pre-committed band
($P{=}\ShufPConfirm{}$) --- but that pool averages \ShufNUp{} checkpoints
\emph{gaining} \ShufUpGain{} points, \ShufNNull{} null, and \ShufDownCk{}
losing \ShufDownLoss{}, intervals excluding zero both ways. Whether ordering or
composition carries the ladder is unresolved (S28).

Above $k\!=\!8$ the cycled control is itself period-8, so that contrast is
$p\!=\!1$ against $p\!=\!8$, not aperiodic text. Never-cycled fillers throughout
remove it: the gap is \ApHeadCk{} by checkpoint and
\ApHeadFam{} by family against \ApHeadCkCyc{} and \ApHeadFamCyc{} cycled,
and we quote the smaller --- though most of that \ApHeadDrop{} points is
vocabulary, not periodicity (\ApHeadTolDrop{} within one unit, nothing on
median error).

\subsection{Not the decoding rule, the judge, or our exclusions}

The families ship repetition penalties differing by an order of magnitude, and a
penalty suppresses repeated tokens directly. Swept on \PenNArch{} architectures
the deficit stays put (XTTS-v2
\PenRepLo{}--\PenRepHi{}\% exact over \PenFold{}-fold, Qwen3-TTS-0.6B
\PenQRepLo{}--\PenQRepHi{}\% over \PenQFold{}, S15), and the \PenNoneN{} Llasa
checkpoints pass \emph{no} penalty and show it at full size. Nor is it
sampling: on Qwen3-TTS-0.6B greedy decoding gives \GreedyGap{} points against
\GreedySampGap{} sampled, and VALL-E~2's repetition-aware
sampling~\cite{chen2024valle2}, firing on \RasFireRep{}\% of steps, leaves
\RasOnGap{} against \RasOffGap{} (S22, S29). Nor our exclusions: with every rule off the gap is
\ExSensAll{} points against \ExSensPanel{}, and the one rule falling unevenly ---
our token budget, at \ExclCapRep{}\% of repeated generations against
\ExclCapCtl{}\% of controls --- censors counts downward, against the contrast
(S18).

Nor is it the recogniser, the objection this design most must answer: CTC
blank-collapse merges adjacent identical words, depressing repeated but not
control counts --- an artifact with the effect's own periodicity signature. Re-scoring the \emph{same} audio with
\IndNJudges{} recognisers --- a second CTC model with different
pretraining, a robust-finetuned one, and Whisper, whose autoregressive decoder
has no blank-collapse mechanism at all --- leaves the gap at
\IndGapLo{}--\IndGapHi{} points, positive in all \IndNCkPos{} of \IndNCk{}
checkpoints and every family under every judge. Decisive is which arm moves:
across them the repeated arm's exact rate spans \IndRepSpread{} points
(\IndRepLo{}--\IndRepHi{}\%) against the control arm's \IndCtlSpread{}.
Changing the scorer moves the arm the models get \emph{right} --- word error
rate --- and leaves the arm they get wrong fixed, where a judge-side collapse
predicts the reverse. Disagreements do concentrate on repeated items, but with
the \emph{opposite} sign to the confound --- $+\IndAsym{}$ where the artifact
requires $\IndAsymThresh{}$ --- so our judge under-states the deficit rather
than manufacturing it (S14). VITS~\cite{kim2021vits} shows \emph{no} dissociation
through the same recogniser on the same strings (\VitsRep{}\% against
\VitsCtl{}\%, $n{=}\VitsN{}$, a gap of \VitsGap{} against the panel's
$+\ARPoolGap{}$), and not for want of competence (S13); blank-collapse would
have depressed its repeated items too.

F5-TTS~\cite{chen2024f5tts}, flow-matching rather than recurrent, \emph{does}
show it: \FivettsRep{}\% against \FivettsCtl{}\%, $+\FivettsGap{}$, so we
withdraw the architectural claim an earlier draft made. What plausibly separates
the two is where the count must live: VITS gives each token its own duration,
F5-TTS estimates one total. Supplying F5-TTS that duration lifts exact
renderings \DurLoFree{}\% to \DurLoFixed{}\% below $k\!=\!\DurSplit{}$ and
\DurHiGain{} at or above it ($n=\DurHiN{}$, gains above \EqDurBound{} points
excluded): handed the right length it still cannot place thirty-two repetitions
in it (S13, S20).

The $k\!\ge\!6$ threshold was chosen after seeing where the arms diverge, which
is why the abstract gives the unconditioned figure too (\FullLadderGap{} points
from $k\!=\!1$) and the specification curve varies it. Two exploratory analyses, dated in S16, are reported in
text alone (S8, S10, S17). Within $k\le32$ the deficit is proportional, not
saturating (RSS \ShapePropSSE{} against \ShapeSatSSE{}), so no horizon lies in
this ladder; extending to $k\!\le\!128$ lowers the fitted saturation
scale \HzRatio{}-fold, but form-dependently (\HzFormLo{}--\HzFormHi{}) and not
unanimously (\HzRevNames{} inverts it). Neither that nor the rate of
effective-rank gain distinguishes a horizon from any saturating process.
